attempts.blocker_detail: On the same warm process, output_length=256 completed c1 and c2, then c4 returned RemoteDisconnected for all four requests; /health and /v1/models returned connection refused afterward and the --rm benchmark containers were gone on Spark4 and Spark5. The preceding 128-token run also saw live Triton JIT for _fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant_per_head, so the next reproduction should preserve container logs and extend warmup coverage before calling this an intrinsic scheduler limit.

do_not_apply: Do not route 256-token c>=4 work to this exact safe c256 launch profile until the c4 API-death reproduction is captured with preserved logs.
Do not run future destructive vLLM stress with docker --rm; it erased the crash logs needed to diagnose the c4/output256 failure.
Do not treat c256 at 128-token output as evidence that 256-token output is stable; the same warm process died at c4 for 256 tokens.
conclusion.next_code_change: Relaunch Spark4/Spark5 TP=2 without --rm and with persistent vLLM logs, extend warmup for _fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant_per_head, then reproduce output_length=256 c4 before retesting c8/c16.

custom_ds4_lessons_tested.lesson: Longer completions amortize request overhead better than 32-token cells.
custom_ds4_lessons_tested.result: Accepted for 128-token completions: c256 reached 328.132 aggregate tok/s versus 163.908 at 32 tokens in the prior standard-runtime artifact.
custom_ds4_lessons_tested.vllm_transfer: Measure output length separately from concurrency when sizing provider lanes.
